main_text.p: libertas fit necessitas. Quod igitur in se li-berum & contingens est, id in sensu com-posito cum conditione & determinatione sive externâ & non vitali, sive interna & vitali, z̃ dicitur necessarium: Atque hoc pacto libere agit homo in sensu diviso & in se: necessariò quatenus & seipsum determinat, & à Deo determinatur; Non ergò hic pugna est necessitatis & libertatis. Sed de his alibi prolixius, in doctrinâ de causa Efficiente.
main_text.head: CAP. VII.
DE
Statu, seu Mutabilitate & Immutabilitate.
main_text.p: 1. Equitur Status, qui est Entis in esse debito perseverantia: Res autem in esse perseverat, vel immutabiliter sine aliquo defectu, vel mutabiliter cum defectu: à priori modo res dicitur immutabilis, à posteriori vero mutabilis.

2. Immutabilitas igitur est modus veritatis, quo Ens habet esse suum sibi debitum, citra defectum perseverans: Quæ per negationem oppositæ differentiæ concipitur definitio, quòd positivæ voces non occurrant.

page.notes: The initial "S" of paragraph 1 is a large woodcut initial, read as "S" joined to "Equitur" (printed "SEquitur"). Marks such as "z̃" in the running text are unclear. The sentence "Equitur" is probably "Aequitur" as printed in the scan; the reading is doubtful. Some words in the head lines are partly obscured by show-through and are uncertain. The line "Statu, seu Mutabilitate & Immutabilitate" is a title in italic display type.
